rv.q: Job is a head-game thriller that delivers an intense experience, deliberately crafted to evoke a deep sense of discomfort about the advancement of technology...
I can't imagine a big venue providing the same intense wallop offered in David Esbjornson's current production in the small black-box space at Writers Theatre.
Still, “Job” is recommended for the great performances, and the excellent production.

cn.t: Critics praise this intense two-hander about a gun-toting therapy patient as a gripping, slow-burn psychological drama that showcases the raw power of live theater, particularly effective in an intimate black-box setting.
